```{r}
need <- c("tidyverse", "lubridate", "zoo",
          "forecast", "TSA", "tseries")
to_install <- need[!suppressWarnings(sapply(need, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE))]
if (length(to_install)) install.packages(to_install, dependencies = TRUE)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(lubridate)
  library(zoo)
  library(forecast)
  library(TSA)
  library(tseries)
})

```

```{r}
## 1. Load data ----
# Make sure these CSVs are in your working directory

lap_raw         <- read_csv("lap_times.csv")
races_raw       <- read_csv("races.csv")
results_raw     <- read_csv("results.csv")
constructors_raw <- read_csv("constructors.csv")

glimpse(lap_raw)
glimpse(races_raw)
glimpse(results_raw)
glimpse(constructors_raw)
```

```{r}
## 2. Identify Ferrari constructorId ----

ferrari_ids <- constructors_raw %>%
  filter(str_detect(tolower(name), "ferrari")) %>%
  pull(constructorId) %>%
  unique()

ferrari_ids
```

```{r}
## 3. Identify Italian Grand Prix (Monza) races ----
# We will approximate Monza using races named "Italian Grand Prix"
# (This is acceptable for the project description: Italian GP at Monza.)

monza_races <- races_raw %>%
  filter(str_detect(tolower(name), "italian grand prix")) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  arrange(year, date)

monza_races %>% select(raceId, year, name, date) %>% print(n = 10)

monza_race_ids <- monza_races$raceId
```

```{r}
## 4. Link Ferrari drivers to Monza races ----
# results table: which drivers were in Ferrari at each race

ferrari_monza_results <- results_raw %>%
  filter(raceId %in% monza_race_ids,
         constructorId %in% ferrari_ids) %>%
  select(raceId, driverId, constructorId)

# link lap times to these Ferrari drivers at Monza
ferrari_monza_laps <- lap_raw %>%
  inner_join(ferrari_monza_results, by = c("raceId", "driverId"))

# attach year and date (for reference)
ferrari_monza_laps <- ferrari_monza_laps %>%
  left_join(monza_races %>% select(raceId, year, date), by = "raceId") %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date))

glimpse(ferrari_monza_laps)

summary(ferrari_monza_laps$milliseconds)
sum(is.na(ferrari_monza_laps$milliseconds))
```

```{r}
## 5. Aggregate to lap-level Ferrari average per race ----
# For each race and lap, take average Ferrari lap time (if both cars exist)

ferrari_monza_lapmean <- ferrari_monza_laps %>%
  group_by(year, date, raceId, lap) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_lap_ms = mean(milliseconds, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_cars      = n(),
    n_missing   = sum(is.na(milliseconds)),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, date, lap)

# How many laps per race?
race_laps <- ferrari_monza_lapmean %>%
  group_by(raceId, year) %>%
  summarise(max_lap = max(lap), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(year)

race_laps

# Choose a common seasonal period = minimum number of laps across all races
# (ensures every race has at least this many laps)
season_L <- min(race_laps$max_lap)
season_L

# Keep only laps up to season_L so each race is a full season
ferrari_monza_lapmean <- ferrari_monza_lapmean %>%
  filter(lap <= season_L)

# number of races (seasons)
n_seasons <- length(unique(ferrari_monza_lapmean$raceId))
n_seasons
```

```{r}
## 6. Build the seasonal time series ----
# Order data by race (year) and lap
ferrari_monza_lapmean <- ferrari_monza_lapmean %>%
  arrange(year, date, lap)

# Extract vector of lap means
monza_vec <- ferrari_monza_lapmean$mean_lap_ms

length(monza_vec)
expected_length <- n_seasons * season_L
expected_length

# If there are missing combos (some laps with no Ferrari car), length may be < expected_length.
# To be safe, convert to a regular ts and then handle NAs.
# First, we will check if length matches.
if (length(monza_vec) != expected_length) {
  warning("Length of data does not equal n_seasons * season_L; some laps might be missing. We'll treat them as NA and interpolate.")
}

# Create a full index of (race season, lap) and merge
season_index_df <- expand.grid(
  season = seq_len(n_seasons),
  lap    = seq_len(season_L)
) %>%
  arrange(season, lap)

# Map raceId/year to season index
race_order <- ferrari_monza_lapmean %>%
  group_by(raceId, year, date) %>%
  summarise(.groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(year, date) %>%
  mutate(season = row_number()) %>%
  select(raceId, year, date, season)

# Merge back lap means with (season, lap)
monza_full <- ferrari_monza_lapmean %>%
  left_join(race_order, by = c("raceId", "year", "date")) %>%
  select(season, lap, mean_lap_ms) %>%
  arrange(season, lap)

# Join with complete index to ensure every (season, lap) pair exists
monza_full <- season_index_df %>%
  left_join(monza_full, by = c("season", "lap")) %>%
  arrange(season, lap)

# Now build ts (may contain NAs)
monza_ts_raw <- ts(monza_full$mean_lap_ms, frequency = season_L)

# Handle missing values with interpolation
anyNA(monza_ts_raw)

monza_ts <- na.approx(monza_ts_raw, na.rm = FALSE)
monza_ts <- na.locf(monza_ts, na.rm = FALSE, fromLast = FALSE)
monza_ts <- na.locf(monza_ts, na.rm = FALSE, fromLast = TRUE)

anyNA(monza_ts)

# Save the prepared series for appendix
monza_prepared_df <- monza_full %>%
  mutate(mean_lap_ms = as.numeric(monza_ts))

write_csv(monza_prepared_df, "seasonal_ferrari_monza_lapseries.csv")
```

```{r}
## 7. Exploratory analysis ----

plot(monza_ts,
     main = "Ferrari Lap Times at Italian GP (Monza)\n(Each season = one race, each cycle = lap 1..L)",
     xlab = "Season-lap index",
     ylab = "Average lap time (ms)")

summary(monza_ts)

hist(monza_ts,
     main = "Histogram of Ferrari Monza Lap Times",
     xlab = "Average lap time (ms)")

boxplot(monza_ts,
        main = "Boxplot of Ferrari Monza Lap Times",
        ylab = "Average lap time (ms)")

# Seasonal plots (by lap within race)
ggseasonplot(monza_ts,
             year.labels = TRUE,
             main = "Seasonal Plot: Lap-by-Lap Pattern within Monza Races")

ggsubseriesplot(monza_ts) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Subseries Plot by Lap (Seasonal Pattern)")
```

```{r}
## 8. Stationarity, nonseasonal & seasonal differencing ----

# Overall trend/level
time_index <- time(monza_ts)
lm_trend <- lm(as.numeric(monza_ts) ~ time_index)

plot(monza_ts,
     main = "Monza Lap Times with Linear Trend",
     xlab = "Time index",
     ylab = "Average lap time (ms)")
abline(lm_trend, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Unit root tests + differencing suggestions
adf.test(monza_ts)

d <- ndiffs(monza_ts)
D <- nsdiffs(monza_ts, m = season_L)

d; D   # so you can see what they are

# Apply NONSEASONAL differencing only if needed
if (d > 0) {
  monza_diff <- diff(monza_ts, differences = d)
} else {
  monza_diff <- monza_ts
}

# Apply SEASONAL differencing only if needed
if (D > 0) {
  monza_diff_seas <- diff(monza_diff, lag = season_L, differences = D)
} else {
  monza_diff_seas <- monza_diff
}

plot(monza_diff_seas,
     main = paste0("Differenced Series (d = ", d, ", D = ", D,
                   ", m = ", season_L, ")"),
     xlab = "Time index",
     ylab = "Differenced lap time (ms)")

adf.test(monza_diff_seas)

```

```{r}
## 9. ACF & PACF for SARIMA identification ----

par(mfrow = c(1,2))
acf(monza_diff_seas, main = "ACF of Differenced Series")
pacf(monza_diff_seas, main = "PACF of Differenced Series")
par(mfrow = c(1,1))
```

```{r}
## 10. Fit candidate SARIMA models ----

# Automatic SARIMA
fit_auto <- auto.arima(monza_ts,
                       seasonal = TRUE,
                       stepwise = FALSE,
                       approximation = FALSE,
                       D = D,
                       max.P = 2, max.Q = 2, max.p = 3, max.q = 3)

fit_auto

# Some manual SARIMA candidates guided by ACF/PACF
fit_011_011 <- Arima(monza_ts,
                     order = c(0, d, 1),
                     seasonal = c(0, D, 1))

fit_110_011 <- Arima(monza_ts,
                     order = c(1, d, 0),
                     seasonal = c(0, D, 1))

fit_111_011 <- Arima(monza_ts,
                     order = c(1, d, 1),
                     seasonal = c(0, D, 1))

fit_011_111 <- Arima(monza_ts,
                     order = c(0, d, 1),
                     seasonal = c(1, D, 1))

# Model comparison: AIC/BIC
model_comp <- tibble(
  Model = c("auto.arima",
            "ARIMA(0,d,1)(0,D,1)[m]",
            "ARIMA(1,d,0)(0,D,1)[m]",
            "ARIMA(1,d,1)(0,D,1)[m]",
            "ARIMA(0,d,1)(1,D,1)[m]"),
  AIC = c(AIC(fit_auto),
          AIC(fit_011_011),
          AIC(fit_110_011),
          AIC(fit_111_011),
          AIC(fit_011_111)),
  BIC = c(BIC(fit_auto),
          BIC(fit_011_011),
          BIC(fit_110_011),
          BIC(fit_111_011),
          BIC(fit_011_111))
)

model_comp %>% arrange(AIC)
model_comp %>% arrange(BIC)

write_csv(model_comp, "seasonal_monza_model_comparison.csv")
```

```{r}
## 11. Residual diagnostics ----

check_model <- function(fit, title = "") {
  cat("\n============================\n")
  cat("Residual diagnostics for:", title, "\n")
  print(summary(fit))
  forecast::checkresiduals(fit)
}

check_model(fit_auto, "auto.arima (seasonal)")
check_model(fit_111_011, "ARIMA(1,d,1)(0,D,1)[m]")
check_model(fit_011_111, "ARIMA(0,d,1)(1,D,1)[m]")

# Choose the best model based on AIC/BIC + diagnostic checks:
fit_best <- fit_auto  # change this if a manual model looks better
```

```{r}
## 12. Train–test split for forecast evaluation ----
# Hold out last K seasons (races), i.e., h = K * season_L observations

season_L  <- frequency(monza_ts)
n_total   <- length(monza_ts)

K <- 2L  # desired number of seasons to hold out
h <- K * season_L

# If we don't have enough data for K full seasons, reduce K/h
if (h >= n_total) {
  # fallback: hold out about 20% of the data, at least one full season
  h <- max(season_L, floor(0.2 * n_total))
  h <- min(h, n_total - season_L)   # leave at least one season for training
}

train_end <- n_total - h

# Simple index-based split (avoids window() issues)
monza_train <- monza_ts[1:train_end]
monza_test  <- monza_ts[(train_end + 1):n_total]

length(monza_train); length(monza_test)

# Fit models on training set
fit_auto_tr <- auto.arima(monza_train,
                          seasonal = TRUE,
                          stepwise = FALSE,
                          approximation = FALSE,
                          D = D)

fit_111_011_tr <- Arima(monza_train,
                        order    = c(1, ndiffs(monza_train), 1),
                        seasonal = c(0, nsdiffs(monza_train, m = season_L), 1))

# Forecast h steps ahead
fc_auto <- forecast(fit_auto_tr, h = length(monza_test))
fc_111  <- forecast(fit_111_011_tr, h = length(monza_test))

# Compare forecast accuracy on the held-out test set
acc_auto <- accuracy(fc_auto, monza_test)
acc_111  <- accuracy(fc_111,  monza_test)

acc_auto
acc_111
```

```{r}
## 13. Final model & forecasting ----

fit_final <- fit_best

# Forecast next K_future Monza races -> K_future * season_L laps
K_future <- 2L
h_future <- K_future * season_L

fc_final <- forecast(fit_final, h = h_future)
fc_final

autoplot(fc_final) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = paste0("Forecast: Ferrari Lap Times at Monza\nNext ", K_future, " Races"),
    x     = "Future time index (lap within race)",
    y     = "Average lap time (ms)"
  )

# Save forecast table
fc_df <- tibble(
  Step      = seq_len(h_future),
  Point_Fc  = as.numeric(fc_final$mean),
  Lower_80  = as.numeric(fc_final$lower[,"80%"]),
  Upper_80  = as.numeric(fc_final$upper[,"80%"]),
  Lower_95  = as.numeric(fc_final$lower[,"95%"]),
  Upper_95  = as.numeric(fc_final$upper[,"95%"])
)

write_csv(fc_df, "seasonal_monza_forecasts.csv")

```
